findings.current: one word echoed in their minds: victory.
findings.defect: The source explicitly describes “victory” as two characters/words (두 글자), but the translation calls it one word.
findings.rationale: The source emphasizes the two-character phrase 승리, so “one word” changes the stated quantity.
findings.replacement: two words echoed in their minds: victory.

findings.current: His descendants, the dragon-blooded heirs, called themselves the Sons of Heaven
findings.defect: The source says the descendants claimed to be 천자, the title “Son of Heaven.” “Sons of Heaven” turns that singular imperial title into a plural designation.
findings.rationale: 천자를 자처하며 means they styled themselves as Son of Heaven; the glossary also specifies “Son of Heaven” for 천자.
findings.replacement: His descendants, the dragon-blooded heirs, claimed the title of Son of Heaven

summary: The translation is broadly faithful, with two small quantity and title-sense discrepancies.
